text:
[NSTG.2.4.2] **Expiry happens at a defined instant: the sweep at pump
entry.** A pass over the cache removes every entry past its deadline and
fires `delete_cb` for each, alongside the fact-TTL sweep that runs at the
same point ([NTST.3.4]).

The alternative — expiring an entry only when something next reads it —
cannot satisfy [NSTG.2.4], and the failure is in exactly the case the
callback exists for: a key written once, its TTL elapsing, nothing ever
reading it again. Under lazy expiry that entry never leaves, its callback
never fires, and a persisting store holds the row for ever. Lazy expiry
does not remove the drift; it makes the drift depend on read traffic.

A read encountering an expired entry must still not return it, so the
read path removes it as a backstop — **and fires the callback when it
does**. Without that, whether an integrator hears about an entry depends
on whether a reader or the sweep reached it first, which is
non-determinism in an observable ([LDET.1.1]), not merely an
inconsistency.

Two consequences worth stating rather than discovering:

- **The order is: fact sweeps, then the cache sweep, then the run.**
  Both sweeps fire callbacks at pump entry, so which goes first is part
  of what an integrator sees, and it is fixed here rather than left to
  an implementation. Facts go first because the fact sweep changes what
  the rules about to run will match against; the cache sweep is
  notification-only and alters nothing the agenda sees, so running it
  first could only move callbacks earlier without changing any
  decision. **Both sweeps read the same instant** — one clock value for
  the whole of pump entry, so no entry can be live for one sweep and
  expired for the other.
- **The sweep costs pump time.** It walks up to the configured key cap
  every pump ([RTCT.7.1]), which the WCET bound must account for rather
  than absorb silently ([RTCT.12.1]).

The sweep is also what makes the behaviour testable: set a short TTL,
advance the clock past it, pump, observe the callback. Before it there
was no instant at which anything was obliged to happen.
